narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Network Map"**

The whole site is printed transit cartography. A pale map paper carries ink-black signage and four thick, saturated line colours, each of which names a discipline (Backend, Frontend, Mobile, Tooling). Content is arranged the way a metro authority arranges information: a map with a key, a station guide, strip maps per line, a timetable, and a terminus. Strip every word away and the system is still recognisable: 10 to 12px coloured strokes on 45° diagonals, white discs with heavy ink rings where lines meet, rectangular end-of-line bars, and alternating fare-zone bands behind them.

Density is calm and wayfinding-first. Type is large, heavy and direct, set in Overpass, a face descended from highway signage; Overpass Mono appears only for dates, years and codes, the way a timetable sets departure times. Depth comes from layered planes (zone bands far, lines and stations mid, labels near) that drift apart with scroll and pointer, never from shadows or blur. Motion is cartographic: strokes draw themselves along their path, stations fade in once the line reaches them, and the station guide's track fills as the reader scrolls. All of it switches off under `prefers-reduced-motion`, and the content reads completely without it.

The build carries one known divergence from its original direction: on the hero map the lines draw on load (a timed CSS stroke animation), while the scroll-tied drawing lives in the station guide. Treat both as part of the system.
keyCharacteristics: Map paper, ink, and four line colours as named roles; nothing else carries hue.
Thick round-capped strokes, 45° diagonals only, white ringed interchanges.
Overpass at weight 800 for every heading; Overpass Mono only for time and codes.
Flat surfaces; depth is parallax between map planes, not shadow.
Ink-filled "signs" with an arrow are the only buttons.
One dark surface, the terminus, where the backend line runs into contact.

rules.name: The Line Colour Rule
rules.body: Red, blue, green and amber each name a discipline. A line colour appears only where that discipline is meant (a stroke, a bullet, a tag, a strip track), with two sanctioned interaction uses: blue for focus and links, red for hover on signs and underlines. No line colour is ever decoration.

rules.name: The Ink On Amber Rule
rules.body: Text set on a line colour is white on red, blue and green, and ink on amber.

rules.name: The Mono Is Time Rule
rules.body: Overpass Mono is reserved for dates, years and codes. Names, roles and prose are always Overpass.

rules.name: The Baseline Lift Rule
rules.body: Overpass sits high in its box, so filled elements carry 2 to 3px more padding on top than on bottom (signs 9/7 and 20/17, tags 3/2, bullets padding-top 0.12em). Keep the asymmetry when adding filled labels.

rules.name: The Paper Map Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats above the paper. Depth is planes sliding against each other, never a cast shadow.

dos: Do give every discipline its line colour (backend-red, frontend-blue, mobile-green, tooling-amber) and use that colour every time the discipline appears.
Do draw connections as thick round-capped strokes (10 to 12px) that turn only at 45°, with white ringed discs at stations.
Do set headings in Overpass 800 with negative tracking, and dates and years in Overpass Mono.
Do keep primary actions as ink signs with an arrow that turn backend red on hover.
Do show keyboard focus as the 3px frontend-blue outline at 3px offset (night-focus on the terminus).
Do switch off stroke drawing, fades, guide fill and parallax under `prefers-reduced-motion`, leaving every element in its final state.
donts: Don't add box shadows, gradients or blur; depth comes from parallax planes and rules.
Don't introduce a hue outside the four line colours, or use a line colour as decoration.
Don't put white text on tooling amber or set amber text on paper.
Don't draw curved or arbitrary-angle lines on the map; 45° diagonals only.
Don't set names, roles or prose in Overpass Mono.
